preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and 1 <= x <= 4e5 for x in [int(stdin.split()[0]), int(stdin.split()[1]), int(stdin.split()[2])])
preconditions.description: Input consists of three integers n, d, k where each is an integer between 1 and 400,000 inclusive.
n, d, and k are positive integers as per problem constraints.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'NO' if (d > n - 1 or (d == 1 and n > 1) or (k == 1 and n > 1)) else stdout.strip() == 'YES' and len([line for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]]) == n - 1
postconditions.description: If no valid tree exists (diameter d is impossible for n vertices, or k=1 and n>1, or d > n-1), output is 'NO'. Otherwise, output is 'YES' followed by exactly n-1 edges forming a valid tree.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in line.split()) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: If output is 'YES', each of the n-1 subsequent lines contains exactly two integers between 1 and n inclusive, representing valid edges.

postconditions.expression: any(all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]]) and len(set().union(*[{(u, v), (v, u)} for u, v in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]]])) == n - 1 and max(diameter_of_tree([tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]], n), key=lambda x: x[1])[1] == d if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: If output is 'YES', the edges form a connected undirected tree (n-1 edges, no cycles) with diameter exactly d, and every vertex has degree at most k. The diameter is computed as the maximum shortest-path distance between any two vertices in the tree.
